label: June 29–July 05
title: “If the Lord Be God, Follow Him” —  1 Kings 12–13; 17

items.text: Even in disarray and separation from covenants, the Lord called Elijah to be a prophet. His life demonstrates that great faith is possible even in adverse circumstances. The Lord responds to faith with public miracles, quiet private miracles, and often, personal revelations known only to the individual through a still small voice.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Christlike leaders serve the people they lead. Rehoboam's mistake was not listening to wise counsel. Attributes like humility, empathy, and a desire to serve would have helped him. We can use these attributes as leaders in our callings and in guiding our own lives.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: An invitation to sacrifice is an opportunity to exercise our faith in Jesus Christ. The widow of Zarephath’s sacrifice, giving her last food to Elijah, brought blessings and strengthened her faith. Sacrifices we make to follow the Savior can deepen our trust in Him and bring His blessings.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Elisha’s actions in dedicating himself to Elijah, much like the widow’s sacrifice, show a profound commitment. These acts teach us that our sacrifices, made with faith in the Savior, are opportunities to grow closer to Him and experience His blessings in our lives.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The Israelites on Mount Carmel might have had reasons to worship Baal, especially during a drought. However, Elijah’s challenge was to choose. This reminds us to consider why we might be indecisive in following the Lord and to commit to Him, as He teaches us who He truly is.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: “If the Lord be God, follow him.” This powerful declaration from Elijah calls us to make a clear choice. What experiences have helped you commit to following the Savior? Consider what the Lord was trying to teach about Himself through Elijah’s ministry.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The Lord often speaks in quiet, simple ways. Elijah’s experience in the wilderness, after the miracle on Mount Carmel, shows that the Lord communicates in ways that meet our needs, even in times of loneliness and discouragement, through a still small voice.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Ponder times when you feel the Lord has spoken to you. His voice can be described as “still” and “small,” requiring us to listen intently. To receive His guidance more often, we need to create stillness and attune ourselves to the promptings of the Spirit.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Using multiple senses can enhance gospel learning. Think of images or sounds to illustrate the words “still” and “small” as you learn about the Lord’s voice. Engaging our senses helps us better understand and remember the quiet ways the Spirit communicates.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The Lord works in quiet, private miracles, often revealing Himself through a “still small voice.” Cultivating the ability to recognize this subtle communication is essential for receiving personal revelation and guidance in our lives, especially when we feel alone or discouraged.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026
